papers.title: Unlocking Lossless Speedups in LLMs via Discrete Diffusion
papers.abstract: Abstract Diffusion-augmented autoregressive language models use parallel token sampling via distilled diffusion weights and a specialized sampler to accelerate inference without quality loss or draft models.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Large Language Models (LLMs) owe much of their success to next-token prediction (NTP), but their autoregressive (AR) structure requires slow, sequential token generation. To overcome this bottleneck, we introduce diffusion-augmented LLMs, a new class of models that defines an AR model distribution while using diffusion to draw multiple tokens in parallel from that distribution. We decouple the parameters of these models into two sets: AR weights, trained using the standard NTP objective, and lightweight diffusion weights, trained to generate multiple tokens simultaneously. The diffusion weights are learned through a simple Diffusion Distillation phase that adds negligible overhead to existing LLM training pipelines. We also introduce Ψ-Spec, a family of samplers that enables lossless acceleration and inference-time scaling at a fixed context length. Unlike speculative decoding, our method requires no separate draft model. Unlike diffusion LLMs (d-LLMs), it accelerates generation without sacrificing the quality of the underlying AR model. The resulting models, called Uno, can be trained from scratch or built by augmenting existing open-weight AR LLMs. Uno achieves higher throughput than leading speculative-decoding methods at every evaluated batch size and delivers up to 3times speedups over the base AR model, including at the largest batch size supported by the device. Notably, our 8B Uno model outperforms the leading open d-LLM, the 26B DiffusionGemma, and the proprietary Mercury 2 across all evaluated benchmarks in agentic tool use, coding, and long-context reasoning. We release code and checkpoints at: https://s-sahoo.github.io/uno/

ru.title: Параллельная генерация токенов через диффузию без потери качества
ru.desc: В работе предложены diffusion-augmented LLM — модели, которые сочетают автрегрессивное предсказание следующего токена с диффузионным процессом для параллельной генерации нескольких токенов одновременно. Модель разделяет параметры на два набора: веса автрегрессивной части, обученные стандартным методом, и лёгкие диффузионные веса, добавленные через специальный этап Diffusion Distillation без значительных затрат на обучение. Авторы представляют семейство семплеров Ψ-Spec, которые обеспечивают ускорение без потери качества и не требуют отдельной модели-черновика в отличие от speculative decoding. Полученные модели Uno достигают ускорения до 3 раз при сохранении качества и превосходят существующие методы диффузионных LLM и speculative decoding по пропускной способности и качеству на различных бенчмарках.

en.title: Accelerating Language Models with Diffusion for Faster Inference
en.desc: This paper presents diffusion-augmented autoregressive language models, which enhance the efficiency of token generation in large language models (LLMs) by allowing parallel sampling. The authors introduce a novel approach that separates model parameters into autoregressive weights and lightweight diffusion weights, enabling simultaneous token generation without compromising quality. Their method, Ψ-Spec, accelerates inference and scales effectively at a fixed context length, outperforming existing speculative decoding techniques. The resulting models, named Uno, demonstrate significant speed improvements and superior performance on various benchmarks compared to other leading models.

zh.title: 扩散增强模型：加速推理的新突破
zh.desc: 本文介绍了一种新的语言模型，称为扩散增强自回归语言模型（Diffusion-augmented autoregressive language models），旨在加速推理过程而不损失质量。该模型通过使用扩散权重和专门的采样器，实现了并行的标记采样，从而克服了传统自回归模型的顺序生成瓶颈。模型的参数被分为两组：自回归权重和轻量级扩散权重，后者通过简单的扩散蒸馏阶段进行训练。最终，Uno模型在多个基准测试中表现优于现有的扩散语言模型，显示出更高的生成速度和效率。

papers.title: FlowBalance: Verifier-Grounded Self-Improvement from On-Policy Reasoning Experience
papers.abstract: Abstract FlowBalance improves reasoning models via verifier-calibrated self-guidance using trajectory-level score reweighting and profile-based trajectory balance.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small A reasoning model can improve from its own on-policy experience, but this inner loop is fragile: terminal verifiers provide reliable yet sparse supervision, while dense same-model guidance can reinforce false confidence or overconcentrate learning on a narrow solution mode. We introduce FlowBalance, a verifier-grounded self-improvement method that learns a normalized distribution over complete responses. For each on-policy trajectory, a frozen training-time view of the same policy uses privileged context to produce token-level log-probability gains, which are aggregated into a trajectory-level self-guidance score. FlowBalance calibrates this score with the verifier-derived group advantage: guidance is retained on positive-advantage trajectories, reversed on negative-advantage trajectories, and disabled when the rollout group provides no outcome preference. The resulting energy exponentially reweights a reference policy, and profiled trajectory balance fits the normalized target with one log-partition estimate per rollout group. This realizes outcome-calibrated self-guidance via trajectory balance, without a separate token-level imitation loss. Our analysis establishes within-group contrast preservation, a minimum-change reverse-KL characterization, monotonic verifier control of target reward, and an exact correction against false-positive self-guidance on rejected responses. On mathematical reasoning, FlowBalance improves average performance over FlowRL on both Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B, while also improving training speed and stability, avoiding direct OPSD's response-length collapse, and exhibiting higher correct-strategy diversity in a controlled AIME24 diagnostic.

ru.title: Самонаведение с калибровкой верификатора через переweighting траекторий
ru.desc: FlowBalance — это метод самосовершенствования модели рассуждения, который использует верификатор для калибровки самогuidance при переобучении на собственном опыте. Метод работает с полными ответами, вычисляя token-level логарифмические вероятностные выигрыши и агрегируя их в траекторий-level score самогuidance. Система калибрует этот score с преимуществом группы из верификатора: guidance сохраняется на положительных траекториях, разворачивается на отрицательных и отключается при отсутствии предпочтения. Профилированный trajectory balance подгоняет нормализованный target через энергетическое переweighting reference policy, достигая лучших результатов в математическом рассуждении без отдельной token-level имитационной потери.

en.title: Enhancing Reasoning Models with Verifier-Calibrated Self-Guidance
en.desc: FlowBalance is a method designed to enhance reasoning models by using a self-guidance approach that is calibrated with verifier feedback. It addresses the challenges of relying solely on on-policy experiences, which can lead to overconfidence in incorrect solutions. By employing trajectory-level score reweighting and balancing based on verifier-derived advantages, FlowBalance ensures that guidance is applied effectively, promoting learning from successful trajectories while avoiding pitfalls from negative ones. This approach not only improves performance in mathematical reasoning tasks but also increases training efficiency and stability, leading to a more robust model.

zh.title: FlowBalance：推理模型的自我改进新方法
zh.desc: FlowBalance是一种通过验证器校准自我指导来改进推理模型的方法。它使用轨迹级得分重加权和基于配置文件的轨迹平衡来实现自我改进。该方法通过对每个轨迹的得分进行校准，确保在正向轨迹上保留指导，而在负向轨迹上则反转指导。实验结果表明，FlowBalance在数学推理任务中显著提高了模型的平均性能和训练速度，同时保持了更高的策略多样性。

papers.title: ENEAS: Embedding-guided Neural Ensemble for Adaptive Segmentation
papers.abstract: Abstract ENEAS unifies text-prompted instance tracking and open-concept semantic discovery via temporal memory extension and a verification layer that filters visual distractors.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small We present ENEAS, a unified, text-promptable method for instance tracking and semantic discovery. Text-promptable segmentation models, including the latest foundation models such as SAM 3, still suffer from temporal hallucinations, spatial fragmentation, and semantic misclassification: they fail to report target absence when an object leaves the field of view, segment local textures instead of the complete object during extreme close-ups, and prioritize visual features over ontological reality, so that visually similar artifacts such as statues, paintings, or reflections are segmented as target entities.   ENEAS works two ways from a single method: precise tracking and high-quality segmentation of a unique instance, and open-concept discovery of every instance a text query names, resolved by a semantic verification layer. For tracking, we extend the geometrically robust SeC architecture, previously limited to point interactions, with a text-prompting adapter and leverage its temporal memory, so that the target is held through disappearance without drifting to distractors and kept whole even when it fills the entire view. For discovery, the verification layer combines high-speed visual embedding matching with conditional VLM refinement, invoking semantic reasoning only for ambiguous candidates, which filters out the ontological errors that visual-only models cannot distinguish while keeping latency low. Designed with 3D reconstruction in mind, where a single misclassified distractor corrupts the asset, ENEAS unlocks high-quality semantic tracking and segmentation of video, of broad libraries, and of collections of temporally or spatially unordered data, together with the discrimination to tell true instances from their doppelgangers: things that look alike but are not the same. The code and models are available at https://github.com/speridlabs/eneas

ru.title: Текстовое отслеживание объектов с семантической верификацией через временную память
ru.desc: ENEAS — это единый метод, который объединяет отслеживание объектов по текстовому описанию и открытое семантическое обнаружение в видео. Система преодолевает ограничения современных фундаментальных моделей, таких как SAM 3, которые страдают от временных галлюцинаций, фрагментации и ошибочной классификации похожих объектов. Метод расширяет архитектуру SeC с помощью адаптера для текстовых запросов и использует временную память, чтобы удерживать целевой объект при его исчезновении из поля зрения. Для различения настоящих объектов от визуально похожих артефактов используется слой верификации, который комбинирует быстрое визуальное сравнение с семантическими рассуждениями VLM.

en.title: ENEAS: Unifying Tracking and Discovery with Text Prompts
en.desc: ENEAS is a novel method that combines instance tracking and semantic discovery using text prompts. It addresses common issues in segmentation models, such as temporal hallucinations and semantic misclassification, by incorporating a verification layer that filters out visual distractions. The method enhances tracking by utilizing a robust architecture that maintains object integrity even when it disappears from view. Additionally, it allows for open-concept discovery of instances based on text queries, ensuring accurate identification of objects while minimizing errors from visually similar artifacts.

zh.title: ENEAS：文本驱动的智能实例跟踪与语义发现
zh.desc: ENEAS是一种统一的文本提示实例跟踪和开放概念语义发现的方法。它通过扩展时间记忆和验证层来过滤视觉干扰，解决了现有模型在时间幻觉、空间碎片化和语义误分类等问题。ENEAS能够实现精确的实例跟踪和高质量的分割，同时支持根据文本查询发现每个实例。该方法结合了快速的视觉嵌入匹配和条件视觉语言模型的细化，确保在低延迟下过滤掉视觉模型无法区分的本体错误。

papers.title: Causal Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Abstract Causal foundation models apply pretrained neural networks to estimate causal effects on new datasets via in-context learning without fine-tuning.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Causal inference is the practice of estimating the effect of a treatment or intervention from data. It traditionally requires a bespoke pipeline for every new problem: first proposing a causal mechanism, selecting a compatible estimator, and finally training it. Meanwhile, across diverse settings and modalities, much of machine learning has shifted to the paradigm of foundation models: networks pretrained once at scale and applied to new tasks without fine-tuning. Causal foundation models (CFMs) bring this paradigm to causal inference. CFMs are pretrained neural networks that estimate causal quantities, such as the average treatment effect, on entirely new datasets using in-context learning without requiring model updates. This work provides a practical introduction to this emerging area. We summarize the necessary background in causal inference and machine learning before discussing CFMs. Throughout, we include example code and Jupyter notebooks.

ru.title: Универсальные нейросети для оценки причинно-следственных эффектов без переобучения
ru.desc: Статья описывает каузальные фундаментальные модели (CFM) — предварительно обученные нейронные сети, которые могут оценивать причинно-следственные эффекты на новых датасетах без дополнительного обучения, используя внутриконтекстное обучение. Традиционный подход к каузальному выводу требует создания отдельного конвейера обработки для каждой задачи, включая выбор механизма причинности и совместимого оценивателя. CFM переносят парадигму фундаментальных моделей, успешно применяемую в современном машинном обучении, на область каузального анализа. Работа служит практическим введением в эту область с предоставлением фонового материала, примеров кода и Jupyter-ноутбуков.

en.title: Revolutionizing Causal Inference with Pretrained Models
en.desc: Causal foundation models (CFMs) leverage pretrained neural networks to estimate causal effects on new datasets without the need for fine-tuning. This approach simplifies the traditional causal inference process, which typically involves creating a specific pipeline for each new problem. By utilizing in-context learning, CFMs can directly apply learned knowledge to estimate causal quantities like average treatment effects. This paper serves as a practical guide to CFMs, providing essential background information and example code for implementation.

zh.title: 因果推断的新方法：基础模型的应用
zh.desc: 因果基础模型（CFMs）利用预训练的神经网络，通过上下文学习在新数据集上估计因果效应，而无需微调。传统的因果推断需要为每个新问题设计特定的流程，包括提出因果机制、选择合适的估计器和训练模型。CFMs将基础模型的理念引入因果推断，使得在不同设置和模态下可以直接应用预训练的网络。本文提供了对这一新兴领域的实用介绍，并包含因果推断和机器学习的必要背景知识。

papers.title: Verify Before You Distill: Prompt-Level Teacher Gating for On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: Abstract Teacher-Gated On-Policy Distillation verifies teacher reliability per prompt via verifier-scored probes, routing to dense distillation or verifier-grounded reinforcement learning to improve training efficiency and accuracy.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small On-policy distillation (OPD) accelerates post-training by providing dense token-level supervision from a frozen teacher on the student's own rollouts. Vanilla OPD applies this supervision uniformly across prompts, without checking whether the teacher is reliable for each prompt. Because reverse KL is mode-seeking, a confidently wrong teacher can induce a strong yet misleading update. Distributional proxies, such as entropy or teacher-student likelihood agreement, measure uncertainty or agreement but do not directly verify outcome correctness. We introduce Teacher-Gated On-Policy Distillation (TGOPD), built on the principle that teacher reliability should be verified at the prompt level before dense supervision is admitted. TGOPD estimates reliability from a small set of verifier-scored teacher probes and routes each prompt exclusively to dense OPD when the reliability check passes or to verifier-grounded GRPO otherwise. Across 4B and 35B students in mathematics, code, and instruction following, TGOPD outperforms Vanilla OPD in all six single-domain settings and achieves higher seven-benchmark averages at both scales under multi-domain training. By using otherwise-idle teacher capacity for reliability estimation, TGOPD also reduces teacher-side compute waste in asynchronous OPD, increasing teacher-node GPU utilization from 9.8% to 78.9% in the measured 4B single-domain run.

ru.title: Проверенная дистилляция: маршрутизация обучения по надёжности учителя
ru.desc: В этой работе предлагается метод Teacher-Gated On-Policy Distillation (TGOPD), который проверяет надёжность учителя для каждого промпта перед применением дистилляции. Система использует верификатор для оценки качества выходов учителя на пробных примерах и маршрутизирует промпты либо на плотную дистилляцию знаний, либо на верификатор-ориентированное обучение с подкреплением. Авторы показывают, что такой подход превосходит стандартную OPD на задачах по математике, программированию и следованию инструкциям для моделей размером 4B и 35B параметров. Кроме того, метод повышает эффективность использования вычислительных ресурсов учителя, увеличивая GPU-утилизацию с 9.8% до 78.9%.

en.title: Verify Before You Distill: Enhancing Teacher Reliability in ML Training
en.desc: The paper introduces Teacher-Gated On-Policy Distillation (TGOPD), a method that improves the training of machine learning models by verifying the reliability of a teacher model for each prompt before applying dense supervision. Unlike traditional On-Policy Distillation (OPD), which applies teacher guidance uniformly, TGOPD assesses the teacher's accuracy using verifier-scored probes, ensuring that only reliable prompts receive dense supervision. This approach not only enhances training efficiency and accuracy but also reduces unnecessary computational waste by optimizing the use of teacher resources. The results show that TGOPD significantly outperforms Vanilla OPD across various tasks, demonstrating its effectiveness in multi-domain settings.

zh.title: 教师门控在线蒸馏：提升训练效率与准确性
zh.desc: 教师门控的在线蒸馏（TGOPD）通过验证器评分探针来检查教师在每个提示下的可靠性，从而提高训练效率和准确性。与传统的在线蒸馏（OPD）不同，TGOPD在提供密集监督之前，先验证教师的可靠性，确保只有在可靠性检查通过时才进行密集蒸馏。TGOPD在数学、代码和指令跟随等多个领域的实验中，均优于传统的OPD方法，显示出更高的性能。通过利用教师的计算能力进行可靠性估计，TGOPD还显著减少了教师端的计算浪费。

papers.title: EmbodiedSkills: A Unified Framework for Orchestrating, Training, and Deploying VLA Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract EmbodiedSkills proposes a unified framework that validates and verifies robot skill executions through a fixed interface, enabling closed-loop embodied agents with adaptable low-level vision-language-action policies.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Vision-language-action (VLA) models map visual observations and language instructions directly to robot actions, but long-horizon tasks require more than action prediction. An agent must coordinate perception, planning, execution, progress verification, and recovery as the physical state evolves. An action prediction or a model-generated skill decision does not, by itself, guarantee that the proposed operation is valid in the current state or that its outcome will be verified. We propose EmbodiedSkills, a unified framework that treats each skill decision as an execution proposal: the runtime checks its prerequisites before execution and verifies the outcome afterward. A shared executable-skill interface connects high-level skill selection, bounded low-level VLA execution, and post-action verification within a single agent loop. Because this interface remains fixed, low-level VLA policies can be replaced or adapted without changing the agent loop. The interface also records planning, execution, verification, and recovery events as structured trajectories, which provide supervision for individual components and can support optional online adaptation when interactive feedback is available. We instantiate EmbodiedSkills with Qwen3-VL and OpenPI/pi0.5 on RoboTwin 2.0 and LIBERO. Task-adapted low-level VLA policies achieve an average success rate of 86.20% across 50 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks and 97.40% across the four LIBERO suites. These results establish the execution performance of the task-adapted low-level VLA policies used in EmbodiedSkills. On four memory-dependent RMBench tasks, the same task-adapted execution approach achieves 12.5% average success. The framework provides a trainable and inspectable agent layer for turning these policies into closed-loop embodied systems.

ru.title: Замкнутые робототехнические агенты через верифицированное исполнение навыков
ru.desc: В статье предлагается EmbodiedSkills — унифицированная архитектура для валидации и верификации выполнения робототехнических навыков через фиксированный интерфейс. Система интегрирует высокоуровневый выбор навыков, низкоуровневое исполнение с использованием vision-language-action моделей и постфактическую проверку результатов в единый замкнутый контур агента. Каждое решение о навыке рассматривается как предложение к выполнению, которое проходит проверку предусловий перед запуском и верификацию результата после завершения. Фиксированный интерфейс позволяет гибко заменять и адаптировать низкоуровневые политики без изменения основного цикла агента, а структурированные траектории выполнения обеспечивают супервизию компонентов и поддерживают онлайн-адаптацию с обратной связью.

en.title: Empowering Robots with Unified Skill Verification
en.desc: EmbodiedSkills introduces a framework for validating and verifying robot skills through a consistent interface, allowing robots to adapt their vision-language-action (VLA) policies. It emphasizes the need for coordination among perception, planning, execution, and verification to handle complex tasks effectively. The framework treats each skill decision as a proposal that is checked for prerequisites and verified post-execution, ensuring that actions are valid in the current context. By maintaining a fixed interface, it allows for easy adaptation of low-level policies while providing structured data for supervision and potential online learning.

zh.title: 统一框架，提升机器人技能执行的可靠性
zh.desc: EmbodiedSkills提出了一个统一框架，用于验证和确认机器人技能的执行。该框架通过固定接口，使得机器人能够在执行过程中适应低级视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略。它将每个技能决策视为执行提案，并在执行前检查其前提条件，执行后验证结果。通过记录规划、执行、验证和恢复事件，EmbodiedSkills为各个组件提供监督，并支持在有交互反馈时的在线适应。

papers.title: One Symptom, Three Levers: A Critical Review of On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.abstract: Abstract On-policy self-distillation for mathematical reasoning uses privileged information to guide a model without a larger teacher, but suffers from reasoning collapse governed by token weighting, privileged context, and guidance dynamics.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small On-policy distillation trains a language model on its own generations while a teacher scores them token by token. It combines the dense supervision of imitation learning with the on-policy sampling of reinforcement learning. But it requires a second, larger model to act as teacher. On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) removes that cost. The teacher is the model itself, conditioned on privileged information the student will not have at test time, such as a reference solution, a plan, or environment feedback. The teacher is no stronger than the student, only better informed. Early results were promising, with accuracy comparable to reinforcement learning at a fraction of the generated tokens. But the same asymmetry that produces the signal also biases it. One failure mode now dominates the field: collapse, the progressive narrowing of the set of reasoning paths the model can produce. Collapse is not specific to OPSD, though privileged information aggravates it. This review treats collapse as a symptom governed by three levers: (i) where the signal is applied, that is, how tokens are weighted; (ii) what the teacher is shown, that is, the nature of the privileged information; and (iii) when the signal changes, that is, the teacher's dynamics and the decay of guidance. We restrict our scope to mathematical reasoning, where the method originated and where its failure modes are best documented. We report no new experiments. The contribution is structural: a shared vocabulary for phenomena named differently across papers, and a clear line between what is settled and what is still disputed.

ru.title: Самодистилляция без учителя: диагностика коллапса рассуждений через взвешивание и информацию
ru.desc: В статье рассматривается метод self-distillation, когда языковая модель обучается на своих собственных генерациях с использованием привилегированной информации (например, эталонного решения или плана), которая недоступна во время инференса. Авторы анализируют проблему коллапса рассуждений — прогрессирующего сужения множества путей вывода, которые может производить модель. Они предлагают единую терминологию для описания этого явления через три ключевых параметра: взвешивание токенов, характер привилегированной информации и динамику обновления сигнала обратной связи. Работа представляет собой систематический обзор без новых экспериментов, фокусируясь на математическом рассуждении и структурировании знаний о механизмах отказа метода.

en.title: Empowering Models with Self-Guidance: Tackling Reasoning Collapse in OPSD
en.desc: This paper discusses On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) for improving mathematical reasoning in language models. OPSD allows a model to learn from its own outputs using privileged information, eliminating the need for a larger teacher model. However, it faces a challenge known as 'collapse', where the model's reasoning paths become limited due to biases in how it receives guidance. The authors propose a framework to understand and address these issues by focusing on the application of signals, the nature of privileged information, and the dynamics of guidance.

zh.title: 在线自蒸馏：数学推理的新方法
zh.desc: 这篇论文讨论了一种名为“在线自蒸馏”的方法，用于数学推理任务。该方法利用特权信息来指导模型，而不需要更大的教师模型，从而降低了成本。尽管早期结果显示准确性与强化学习相当，但模型推理路径的逐渐收窄现象（称为崩溃）仍然是一个主要问题。论文还提出了影响崩溃的三个因素：信号应用的位置、教师所见的特权信息的性质以及信号变化的时机。

papers.title: Unifying Conformal Language Tasks with In-Context Ensembles
papers.abstract: Abstract The Conformal Relevance framework automates score function design for conformal prediction via in-context learning and ensembling to improve conciseness while preserving coverage across NLP retrieval tasks.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Many NLP tasks, such as summarization and extractive question answering, reduce to retrieving relevant content from documents under two constraints: coverage, retaining enough pertinent information to achieve some goal, and conciseness, removing as much irrelevant information as possible. Conformal prediction methods have been used to guarantee coverage, and must be optimized for conciseness through design of a score function. State-of-the-art scoring functions use hand-engineered LLM prompts asking the model to rate the importance of content, but manual prompt engineering is labor-intensive and task-specific. We introduce the Conformal Relevance framework which uses in-context learning example curation and ensembling to create a score function which maintains coverage while improving conciseness with minimal manual input. We demonstrate this framework's application on seven NLP tasks, and also theoretically study the impact of diversity for ensembled conformal scores, giving a complementarity condition that characterizes when ensembling improves worst-case sentence scores, and a saturation bound on ensemble improvement.

ru.title: Автоматическое конструирование функций оценки релевантности через конформное предсказание
ru.desc: В работе предлагается Conformal Relevance — фреймворк, который автоматизирует разработку функции оценки для конформного предсказания с использованием обучения в контексте и ансамблирования. Метод позволяет улучшить лаконичность текстов при сохранении полноты информации в задачах информационного поиска NLP. Вместо ручной настройки промптов для больших языковых моделей, фреймворк использует подбор примеров в контексте и комбинирование нескольких оценивающих функций с минимальной ручной работой. Авторы теоретически изучают влияние разнообразия в ансамблях и демонстрируют применение подхода на семи различных NLP задачах.

en.title: Automating Score Function Design for Better NLP Retrieval
en.desc: The Conformal Relevance framework enhances conformal prediction in natural language processing (NLP) by automating the design of score functions. It focuses on two key aspects: coverage, which ensures that enough relevant information is retained, and conciseness, which aims to eliminate irrelevant content. Traditional methods rely on manually crafted prompts for scoring, which can be tedious and specific to each task. This framework leverages in-context learning and ensembling techniques to create effective score functions with less manual effort, demonstrating its effectiveness across multiple NLP tasks.

zh.title: 自动化设计评分函数，提升NLP任务的简洁性与覆盖率
zh.desc: 本论文提出了一个名为“Conformal Relevance”的框架，旨在通过上下文学习和集成方法自动化设计评分函数，以提高自然语言处理（NLP）任务中的简洁性，同时保持覆盖率。许多NLP任务，如摘要生成和提取式问答，主要依赖于在保证信息覆盖的同时，去除不相关的信息。传统的保守预测方法需要通过设计评分函数来优化简洁性，而现有的评分函数通常依赖于手工设计的提示，这种方法既费时又特定于任务。我们展示了该框架在七个NLP任务中的应用，并理论研究了集成评分的多样性影响，提供了一个互补条件，描述了何时集成可以改善最坏情况下的句子评分。

papers.title: Safety for Whom? Boundary-Aware Self-Distillation for Controlled LLM Safety Refusal
papers.abstract: Abstract Narrow-boundary safety alignment uses self-generated refusal data and boundary-pair training to precisely control refusal boundaries, improving targeted refusal while reducing over-refusal and harmful responses.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Safety alignment is usually posed as a topic-level question: is this subject harmful? Deployments ask a narrower one. A civics tutor and a public-sector assistant may share a base model yet need different boundaries inside the same topic, refusing targeted political manipulation while still answering factual questions about the same election. We formulate this as narrow-boundary safety and introduce an offline self-generated framework combining controlled topic generation, coverage repair, in-distribution compensation data, and harmful-benign pairs for training and evaluation. Single-shot generation leaves 19.88% of prompts without accepted refusal traces, whereas escalating retries leave 0.20%. On political persuasion with Qwen3-8B, training on refusal data completed through Escalate increases target-domain refusal from 9.47% to 84.75% and reduces the mean unsafe-response rate across three broader harmfulness benchmarks from 26.26% to 0.14%, but increases XSTest over-refusal from 2.00% to 74.00%. In a separate matched comparison, replacing external responses with verified target-model responses reduces over-refusal from 15.20% to 5.20%. Boundary-pair data reduces comply-side over-refusal on held-out pairs from 32.94% to 4.16%, while harmful-side refusal decreases only from 91.88% to 87.72%. These results show that data composition controls the safety and usability trade-off, and that safety alignment should be evaluated on both sides of the intended refusal boundary.

ru.title: Точная настройка границ безопасности: от общих ограничений к узконаправленному контролю
ru.desc: В работе предложен метод узкобoundary safety alignment для точного контроля границ отказов языковых моделей. Авторы разработали фреймворк самогенерируемых данных отказов с использованием контролируемой генерации тем и парных данных для обучения. Метод позволяет значительно улучшить целевые отказы (с 9.47% до 84.75%) при одновременном снижении вредоносных ответов, однако требует балансировки между отказом и переизбыточным отказом. Результаты показывают, что композиция обучающих данных критически влияет на компромисс между безопасностью и полезностью модели.

en.title: Precision in AI Refusals: Balancing Safety and Usability
en.desc: This paper introduces a method called narrow-boundary safety alignment, which focuses on managing how AI systems refuse to answer certain questions. By using self-generated refusal data and a technique called boundary-pair training, the approach aims to improve the accuracy of refusals while minimizing unnecessary refusals and harmful responses. The study demonstrates that this method can significantly increase the rate of appropriate refusals in specific contexts, such as political discussions, while also reducing unsafe responses. Overall, the findings highlight the importance of carefully curating training data to balance safety and usability in AI systems.

zh.title: 精准控制拒绝边界，提升安全对齐效果
zh.desc: 这篇论文提出了一种狭边界安全对齐的方法，通过自生成拒绝数据和边界对训练，精确控制拒绝边界。这种方法提高了针对性拒绝的效果，同时减少了过度拒绝和有害反应的发生。研究表明，使用这种框架可以显著提高在特定领域的拒绝率，并降低不安全反应的比例。最终结果显示，数据组合在安全性和可用性之间的权衡中起着关键作用，安全对齐需要在预期拒绝边界的两侧进行评估。

papers.title: What Else Needs Fixing? Exploring Cost-Effective Test-Time Compute for Revision Propagation in Artifacts Generated Through Conversation
papers.abstract: Abstract  Large Language Models (LLMs) often help users generate artifacts through iterative cycles of generation and revision in conversation. A challenge here is that, when users specify only a local change during revision, LLMs must instead identify the relevant dependencies and propagate the revision to all affected parts of the artifact. This paper studies this ability of LLMs on conversationally generated artifacts, where the artifact context and its dependencies may be embedded in the conversation history. Toward practical use, we also explore cost-effective test-time compute for this new setting. Specifically, we introduce a new benchmark for this setting, and evaluate nine revision methods, including sequential reflection and parallel sampling variants, using gpt-oss-20b/120b, gpt-5.4-mini, and qwen3.5-9b/27b/122b on the benchmark. The results show that baselines achieve accuracies of 68.3--93%, and the most cost-effective method is selecting from three parallel samples using either LLM-based or medoid selection, which improves accuracy by 2.2--9.7%. Our code and dataset are available at https://github.com/ntt-dkiku/llm-revision-propagation.

ru.title: Распространение правок в артефактах: как LLM правильно обновляет зависимые части
ru.desc: В работе исследуется способность больших языковых моделей распространять локальные изменения на все зависимые части артефакта при итеративном редактировании в диалоговом формате. Авторы предлагают новый бенчмарк для оценки этой задачи и сравнивают девять методов ревизии, включая последовательную рефлексию и параллельную выборку. Экспериментальные результаты показывают, что базовые методы достигают точности 68,3-93%, а наиболее экономичный подход заключается в выборе из трёх параллельных образцов с использованием LLM-основанного или медоидного отбора. Этот метод улучшает точность на 2,2-9,7% при оптимальном использовании вычислительных ресурсов на этапе инференса.

en.title: Enhancing Artifact Revisions with LLMs: Efficient Dependency Propagation
en.desc: This paper investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) can effectively manage revisions in artifacts generated through conversation. It highlights the challenge of propagating local changes to all relevant parts of an artifact, which requires understanding the dependencies within the conversation history. The authors introduce a new benchmark to evaluate various revision methods, including sequential and parallel approaches, using different LLMs. Results indicate that the most efficient method improves accuracy significantly while maintaining cost-effectiveness during test-time computation.

zh.title: 提升大型语言模型修订能力的研究
zh.desc: 大型语言模型（LLMs）在对话中通过生成和修订的迭代循环帮助用户生成作品。一个挑战是，当用户仅指定局部更改时，LLMs必须识别相关依赖关系并将修订传播到作品的所有受影响部分。本文研究了LLMs在对话生成作品中的这种能力，并引入了一个新的基准来评估九种修订方法。结果表明，基线方法的准确率为68.3%到93%，最具成本效益的方法是从三个并行样本中选择，准确率提高了2.2%到9.7%。

papers.title: Privacy Failure in Split-LLM Training, The Returned Gradient Nullifies the Decoys
papers.abstract: Abstract A split-LLM training system passed privacy checks but leaked real data rows through zero-gradient patterns, allowing token recovery attacks despite gradient clipping and noise.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small We present a systems-security case study of a two-node split-LLM training system whose privacy evaluation passed while leaving an observable channel untested. The Trusted Local Node (TLN) sends protected activations to the Untrusted Cloud Node (UCN), the UCN returns its output, and TLN, holding the private loss, returns the output gradient. The frame the UCN receives mixes real rows with decoys, and the loss ignores the decoys. Their gradients are exactly zero, so the pattern of zeros reveals which rows were real. We measure it with a protocol fixed in advance: a leak injected at known strength to prove the instrument can see one, a shuffled-label control to prove it does not report absent leaks, and a threshold set before the runs. Across nine seeds, the zeros identified the real rows on every frame, 4,096 of 4,096 per run. An attack on the frame contents recovered about one extra token per hundred over a constant-guess baseline (+0.65 to +1.50 percentage points); the shuffled controls recovered nothing. A second set of runs repeated this on a configuration that keeps model quality within budget, so the finding is not confined to a setting nobody would deploy. On both datasets, every such run passed the forward-channel privacy check and the quality check, yet failed that same check once the returned gradient was included. Clipping and noising each row of the gradient closed the leak for about 0.01 nats of held-out cross-entropy. The system is not thereby safe: five classes of attack, including those accumulating observations across training steps, were never measured.

ru.title: Приватность, которую не видели: нулевые градиенты как канал утечки данных
ru.desc: В статье описывается уязвимость системы распределённого обучения LLM, где большие языковые модели обучаются на двух узлах — защищённом локальном и облачном. Исследователи обнаружили утечку конфиденциальной информации через паттерны нулевых градиентов: когда система смешивает реальные данные с фиктивными примерами, градиенты фиктивных данных остаются нулевыми, открывая информацию о том, какие строки данных были настоящими. Несмотря на прохождение стандартных проверок приватности и применение техник обрезания (clipping) и добавления шума к градиентам, злоумышленник смог восстановить дополнительные токены из исходных данных. Авторы подчёркивают, что найденный канал утечки остался незамеченным при оценке безопасности, и существуют ещё несколько классов атак, которые не были измерены.

en.title: Uncovering Hidden Data Leaks in Split-LLM Training Systems
en.desc: This paper discusses a split-LLM training system that, while passing privacy evaluations, still leaked sensitive data through identifiable zero-gradient patterns. The system consists of a Trusted Local Node (TLN) and an Untrusted Cloud Node (UCN), where the TLN sends protected data to the UCN, which then returns outputs. Despite using techniques like gradient clipping and noise addition, the zero-gradient patterns allowed attackers to identify real data rows among decoys. The study highlights that even systems that seem secure can have vulnerabilities, particularly when certain channels are not adequately tested.

zh.title: 分布式大语言模型训练的隐私风险
zh.desc: 这篇论文讨论了一种分布式大语言模型（LLM）训练系统的安全性问题。尽管该系统通过了隐私检查，但由于零梯度模式的存在，仍然泄露了真实数据行，导致了令牌恢复攻击。系统中，受信任的本地节点（TLN）将保护过的激活发送到不受信任的云节点（UCN），而UCN返回输出，TLN则返回输出梯度。研究表明，零梯度的模式可以揭示哪些行是真实的，尽管系统在隐私检查中表现良好，但在返回梯度时却暴露了隐私风险。
